title: Smooth convex optimization with different domain and smoothness norms
formal: For each fixed \(1\leq p<q\leq\infty\) and \(1<\kappa\leq2\), determine the optimal worst-case error \(\mathcal R_{p,q,\kappa}(n,T)\), up to constant factors, of deterministic algorithms making \(T\) exact first-order queries to minimize a convex function whose gradient is Hölder continuous in the \(\ell_q\) geometry over the unit \(\ell_p\) ball. The target covers every integer \(n\geq2\) and \(1\leq T\leq n\).
why: The problem isolates whether the geometry of a constrained model can improve the fundamental convergence rate when smoothness is measured differently. Matching bounds would explain which gains in sparse and structured regression follow from geometry alone and which require access to additional problem structure.
status_note: The selected cross-norm problem is open in the 2015 source. Later-work checks on 13 September 2026 did not identify matching rates for the full first-order family; the 2026 proximal-oracle result uses different access. This is a dated source-backed status, not an exhaustive proof of current openness.

progress.text: Guzmán poses the cross-norm minimax problem and documents gaps for p below q.
Adil and coauthors give improved and optimal rates for stronger norm-dependent proximal access; this does not by itself determine the first-order cross-norm risk.

sentences: Smooth convex optimization is often analyzed when the objective's regularity and the feasible region use compatible norms.
The source instead studies settings where these geometries differ, including vector norms and their matrix counterparts.
It asks for the optimal oracle complexity of minimizing such functions using black-box first-order information.
The stated gaps concern how smoothness, domain geometry, dimension, and target accuracy interact.
Matching algorithms and lower bounds would show whether sparse and low-rank optimization models permit faster convergence than methods designed around a single common norm suggest.

definitions:
For \(1\leq s<\infty\), put \(\|x\|_s=(\sum_{i=1}^n|x_i|^s)^{1/s}\), and put \(\|x\|_\infty=\max_i|x_i|\). Write \(B_p^n=\{x:\|x\|_p\leq1\}\). The conjugate exponent \(q_*\) is defined by \(1/q+1/q_*=1\), with \(1/\infty=0\). Let \(\mathcal F_{q,\kappa}^n\) be the class of all continuously differentiable convex functions \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) such that \[\|
abla f(x)-
abla f(y)\|_{q_*}\leq\|x-y\|_q^{\kappa-1}\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb R^n).\] There is no bound on the affine part of \(f\), no strong-convexity assumption and no promise of a sparse minimizer. One oracle query at any \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) returns the exact pair \((f(x),
abla f(x))\). A deterministic algorithm chooses each query as a function of the parameters and previous answers, and after at most \(T\) queries outputs \(\widehat x\in B_p^n\). It receives no explicit formula, data matrix, decomposition, proximal oracle or higher derivative. All computation between queries is free and unrestricted; arbitrary deterministic decision maps depending on \(n,T,p,q,\kappa\) are allowed, with no uniformity or bit-precision restriction. Its error is \(f(\widehat x)-\min_{x\in B_p^n}f(x)\). Define \(\mathcal R_{p,q,\kappa}(n,T)=\inf_A\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_{q,\kappa}^n}[f(\widehat x_A(f))-\min_{B_p^n}f]\). Allowing an output outside the ball with error infinity gives the same definition. The minimum of each function exists because the ball is compact. The infimum over algorithms need not be attained. A Hölder bound with constant \(L>0\) and a feasible ball of radius \(R>0\) scales this risk by \(LR^\kappa\).
answer_criterion: Give a noncircular rate \(G_{p,q,\kappa}(n,T)\) and a complete Lean-checked proof of \(c_{p,q,\kappa}G\leq\mathcal R\leq C_{p,q,\kappa}G\) over the entire stated domain, with positive constants independent of \(n,T\). The upper bound may be approached arbitrarily closely if the minimax infimum is not attained. Both the query and dimension dependence, including any logarithmic factors needed for constant-factor matching, must be established. A result for one pair of norms or for a stronger oracle alone does not characterize this family.

context_blocks.text: Guzmán’s 2015 Open Problem 1 asks for large-scale minimax rates when the feasible ball and the smoothness norm differ. This card explicitly selects the vector case \(p<q\), where the reported gaps are substantial, and exact value-and-gradient access. The source also discusses matrix Schatten norms and a more general class of local oracles; those are related extensions rather than additional requirements.

When \(p<q\), the unit \(\ell_p\) ball is contained in the unit \(\ell_q\) ball. The source asks whether algorithms can exploit this smaller feasible geometry more effectively than methods analyzed only in the smoothness norm.

For \(p=1,q=2,\kappa=2\), the source compares an accelerated \(O(T^{-2})\) upper bound with a lower bound of order \(T^{-3}\), up to logarithmic factors, in its large-scale regime. These are dated nonmatching bounds, not a claimed present-day formula for the minimax risk.

Convex regression over a norm-constrained predictor class motivates the problem. Access to the complete regression data can supply structure unavailable to a first-order black box, so a faster algorithm for one explicit regression loss does not automatically determine this oracle complexity.

Adil, Bullins, Jambulapati and Sidford’s 2026 work studies stronger norm-dependent proximal oracles that solve a regularized minimization problem in one call. Its accelerated rates and matching span-restricted lower bounds concern that different information model.

The precision requested here concerns asymptotic error rates as the query budget and dimension vary. It is not an additive numerical tolerance on the risk. Constants may depend on the fixed norm and smoothness exponents; dependence on dimension cannot be hidden there.
